comment: Each verdict compares a Lean-owned own-body semantic target and exact paper-local declaration with its selected byte-pinned paper-source bundle. These are semantic prerequisites, not additional paper-claim rows.

GGRS26CombattingGerrymanderingRCV.Ballot.reason: The record makes explicit the active candidates, elected count, voter weights, and legality conditions needed to carry out the source's iterative count and transfers.

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
In Single Transferable Vote (STV), a type of ranked choice voting for multiple winners, each
voter instead submits a ranking over candidates (here, we assume the rankings are complete, not
partial). Consider a district with Nk seats and Vk voters; the set of winners is created iteratively, as
follows. The number of first-place votes for each candidate is counted. Any candidate with a number
of votes at least the “Droop” threshold Q = ⌊ NVk k+1 ⌋ + 1 is selected as a winner, and their surplus
votes (number of votes minus Q) are transferred to each voter’s next preference. If no candidate has
enough votes, then the candidate with the least number of votes (with tie-breaking) is eliminated,
and their votes are transferred. The process continues until Nk candidates have been selected, or
the number of remaining candidates equals the number of remaining seats. STV is commonly used
in practice in multi-winner elections.
    Details can differ in how such votes are transferred, but our results in Section 3 do not depend
on the transfer rule; in our simulations in Section 4 and Appendix B, we use the “fractional” STV
rule, in which each voter keeps a fractional number of votes equal to their share of the winning
candidate’s surplus votes (we describe this formally in Section 4). For consistency, for all rules we
assume that ties are broken in favor of candidates from party D, but randomly within each party.5

GGRS26CombattingGerrymanderingRCV.Ballot.reason: The source begins the STV analysis with the district's voters and candidates before any winners are selected. The Lean definition constructs that initial active/elected state from those inputs and the initial ballot weights.
The source terminates when all seats are filled or the remaining candidates fill the remaining seats. The Lean predicate is exactly that terminal condition for a ballot-routed STV state.

GGRS26CombattingGerrymanderingRCV.ballot.reason: Proposition 1 measures the Republican winners under STV. The Lean function counts exactly the final elected candidates belonging to the designated party.

GGRS26CombattingGerrymanderingRCV.paper_.reason: Proposition 1 assumes that every party voter ranks all same-party candidates above all others. The Lean predicate records that complete solid-coalition ballot condition.
Lemma C.1 states the unique integer in the half-open interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1). The Lean predicate is that exact interval condition.
Lemma C.1 selects the leftmost maximizer of the displayed PAV harmonic objective over the district's seat counts. The Lean predicate records feasibility, maximality, and the leftmost tie-break.

Lemma C.1 displays the PAV objective as the party vote share times the harmonic score of its chosen seats plus the other party share times the harmonic score of the remaining seats. The Lean definition is that displayed objective.

The source starts from the district's voters, candidates, seats, and solid-coalition rankings before applying STV. The Lean definition constructs that initial ballot-routed state from those same inputs.
Proposition 1 concludes that each Republican seat count is one of floor(y_R M) and ceil(y_R M). The Lean predicate is exactly this rounded-seat-share alternative.

GGRS26CombattingGerrymanderingRCV.pavSea.reason: Lemma C.1's unique-integer condition is exactly the half-open interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1) that this Lean predicate states over the paper's integer variable.

GGRS26CombattingGerrymanderingRCV.seatSh.reason: Proposition 1 states that the Republican STV and PAV winner counts both lie in the floor-or-ceiling set for the party vote share times the number of seats. This predicate is that rounding condition.
